While it is true that labeled data can help improve the accuracy of a language model, it is not necessarily unsafe to use unlabeled data. Unsupervised learning techniques, such as those used in language modeling, often rely on large amounts of unlabeled data. The assistant's claim that unlabeled data may be "contaminated with outliers" is misleading, as outliers can exist in both labeled and unlabeled data.
